{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=metric+temporal+logic+frameworks+for+formal+adversarial+scenario+generation+in+autonomous+epistemic+testing&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.31979/etd.vqbt-kwk2\", \"title\": [\"Uncovering Weaknesses in Autonomous Driving\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31979/etd.vqbt-kwk2\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1305/ndjfl/1040046088\", \"title\": [\"Minimal Temporal Epistemic Logic\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>In the study of nonmonotonic reasoning the main emphasis has been on static (declarative) aspects. Only recently has there been interest in the dynamic aspects of reasoning processes, particularly in artificial intelligence. We study the dynamics of reasoning processes by using a temporal logic to specify them and to reason about their properties, just as is common in theoretical computer science. This logic is composed of a base temporal epistemic logic with a preference relation on models, and an associated nonmonotonic inference relation, in the style of Shoham, to account for the nonmonotonicity. We present an axiomatic proof system for the base logic and study decidability and complexity for both the base logic and the nonmonotonic inference relation based on it. Then we look at an interesting class of formulas, prove a representation result for it, and provide a link with the rule of monotonicity.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1305/ndjfl/1040046088\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1996, 4, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1215/00294527-2024-0009\", \"title\": [\"A Temporal Epistemic Deontic Logic\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Within legal contexts, a claim to knowledge requires that the evidence appealed to fulfills conditions established by legal norms that belong to the so-called Evidence Law. In addition, the epistemic justification presupposed by this kind of knowledge is temporally affected by the changing character of the evidence and the judicial discretion usually exercised in the applications of the Evidence Law. As such, these two scenarios involve three modalities: temporal, epistemic, and deontic. The present paper philosophically discusses the links between these modal dimensions in the above legal context. Based on the discussion, a formal tense-epistemic-deontic logic is developed. That is, the paper characterizes a formal language formally representing the three dimensions through specific logical operators, constructs a formal semantics for the language, and specifies a formal logical system. Finally, the soundness and completeness of the system with respect to the semantics is proved.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1215/00294527-2024-0009\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 8, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-94-007-0074-1_3\", \"title\": [\"Dynamic Epistemic Logic and Temporal Modality\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-007-0074-1_3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2010, 12, 1]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "3140295a1071a7773fac99f5322e0b66d92d4c6b8096422cfdde5e7a99b66404", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.31979/etd.vqbt-kwk2", "doi:10.1305/ndjfl/1040046088", "doi:10.1215/00294527-2024-0009", "doi:10.1007/978-94-007-0074-1_3"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.31979/etd.vqbt-kwk2", "https://doi.org/10.1305/ndjfl/1040046088", "https://doi.org/10.1215/00294527-2024-0009", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-007-0074-1_3"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
